purpose: Boot and flash success criteria as checks rather than prose. Prose describing a good boot has drifted repeatedly in this project: it claimed eight services when there were thirty-four, recorded the chime as failed after it played, and the ring count as unexplained after it was explained. A check cannot drift silently. If the runtime changes, the check fails and names what changed.

evidence.note: An earlier revision cited flash-05811b-2114, which does not exist. The citation was written from memory rather than from the directory listing, which is the same failure the criteria exist to prevent.

boot.why: The MCU service reached the end of DAC initialisation. Nothing else in the boot works without it.
The front lamp is driven at boot, before the network is up.
Wi-Fi associated and the lamp followed. Proves the network path, not just the lamp.
The DSP loaded its firmware and announced itself over SPI.
A level actually reached the DSP. Without it the speaker plays at whatever gain the DSP powered up with, which is inaudible in practice.

The chime rendered. This line is NOT proof of sound: it was logged for weeks while the speaker was silent, because the cue ran before the DSP was up. Necessary, not sufficient. The listener check is the proof.
A skipped cue means the DSP never accepted a level within the timeout.
The ring follows volume changes, as the donor did. Drawing it on every apply attempt made the boot illumination count a readout of DSP latency.
Omitting the Bluedroid config produced a complete-looking build with no identifiers binary. Every volume apply failed and the chime never played.
No softvol plugin exists on this runtime and the default pointed at the Loopback card, so the fade failed on every volume change.

device.why: Thirty-four on a healthy 05.8.11 boot. A build missing Bluedroid showed twenty-eight and reported success everywhere else.
The gadget driver ships this default. A unit still reporting it has never been configured, and adb -s cannot address one of several.
The gadget driver ships the product string Android. A unit reporting it has never been configured, so several speakers are indistinguishable in adb devices and in dmesg.

The gadget driver ships the manufacturer string Android. android_bind writes placeholders into all three descriptor strings and exposes the attributes so the product replaces them; two of the three were replaced for a while and this one was missed.

flash.why: A device that has not entered recovery asks for 0x08 and resumes its normal boot once answered. Serving it cost twelve consecutive failed entries; withholding it reached iROM on the next attempt.
07_IMAGE is a four-byte little-endian size of 83_IMAGE. The known-good copy carries the size of 82_IMAGE instead, which does not apply.
The iROM took the bootstrap. Subclass is NOT the signal: successful traces include both FE and FF, and treating FF as a gate caused a live flash to be reported as a failure.
The U-Boot prompt. The console driver waits for this before sending anything, so without it nothing can be written.

The write command reached the device. The single-stage arm logs "sent l2nand 83"; the two-stage seize logs "writing NAND: l2nand 83". Naming only the first reported the 05.8.13 flash, which worked, as a failure.
The only line that means NAND was written. Repeated 0x08 requests before it are normal and do not indicate failure.

listener.why: A person hears the startup chime. No log line establishes this: CUE_PLAYED was logged for weeks while the speaker was silent.
A person sees the boot swirl and no volume arc.
A person hears no pops during startup. Opening the outputs during initialisation put the amplifier live for DSP bootup and the first gain change, which was audible on this unit.
